important_finding.title: A retained A scrape is attached to a B Diagnose result
important_finding.reproduction: Capture document A in Scrape, reload the tab to same-URL document B without capturing B, launch Diagnose on B and pick an element, then choose Copy for AI. The B picker session and result pass their pageKey checks, but the copied bundle includes A's article markdown and extractor as the current scrape comparison.
important_finding.source_evidence: ScrapeView.tsx:86-88 withholds retained A from the main capture and Save controls. DiagnoseCard.tsx:25-35 checks the result pageKey but reads store.current independently; lines 48-55 pass that unguarded current into formatDiagnoseBundle. diagnose-bundle.ts:227-230 labels B's page and extractor, and lines 275 onward compare B's picked text against that supplied markdown.
important_finding.remedy: Use the same pageKey admission for the scrape supplied to DiagnoseCard; when B has no capture, pass null markdown/extractor and preserve the honest no-current-scrape wording. Add an A/B same-URL Diagnose copy regression through the real card and bundle formatter.

secondary_source_risk.title: An old pre-send refresh can change B's shared cache status
secondary_source_risk.evidence: refresh-page-context.ts:171-225 uses one unowned store.inFlight flag. An A deep capture returning after B activation sets lastError at lines 187-193 even when pageKey is stale, and its finally at line 226 clears inFlight while B's refresh can still be active. The cache record itself is pageKey guarded. This is a status/concurrency gap, not proven stale soup admission.
secondary_source_risk.remedy: Bind inFlight/error ownership to the initiating page and run before updating shared status; test overlapping A/B refreshes.
